anti_overlap: Focuses on MCP protocol surface; fd-query-template-protocol-design covers Python internals; fd-queryresult-serialization-contract covers the data format
decision_lens: Can an agent that has never seen this codebase discover and correctly invoke each named query from the tool listing alone?
focus: MCP tool schema and description quality for cold agent discoverability
name: fd-mcp-tool-schema-discoverability
persona: MCP protocol specialist who has built tool discovery systems and knows how agents parse tool listings
review_areas: Tool descriptions distinguish overlapping queries (who_touched_file vs actor_activity)
Parameter schemas use canonical ID format consistently across all 8 tools
Required vs optional parameters are correctly marked (limit/offset should be optional)
Return type schemas are specific enough for agents to parse without guessing
Tool names follow MCP naming conventions and are unambiguous
Error responses are structured and distinguishable from empty results

severity_examples.condition: who_touched_file and actor_activity descriptions overlap without distinguishing scope
severity_examples.scenario: Two tools have near-identical descriptions making agents pick the wrong one

severity_examples.condition: Agent passes native_id instead of subsystem:native_id format
severity_examples.scenario: canonical_id parameter format not documented in schema

severity_examples.condition: entity_timeline returns 10K+ events with no pagination
severity_examples.scenario: Missing limit parameter causes unbounded result sets

success_hints: Each tool has a unique, action-oriented description. Parameter schemas include format hints. Return schemas are typed.
task_context: Named queries are the primary surface agents use to access the ontology. Poor discoverability defeats the entire purpose of individual tools over a generic query interface.
